title: API key is shipped in client code and sent as a bearer token from the browser
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain script. The constant is global and is attached to every request at api.js:6 and api.js:11.
failing_case: Open the page, view source or the network tab: the key and the Authorization header are visible to every visitor. Anyone can call /refunds with it.
remediation: Move the key to a server or backend-for-frontend that authenticates the user and enforces refund permissions. Rotate the key that was shipped.

title: refund() returns ok:true without awaiting or checking the request, so failed refunds show as success
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await and discards the promise. api.js:12 returns a constant. app.js:51 shows the toast on r.ok. Driven: with the refunds endpoint answering HTTP 500, the toast still read 'Refunded 3 orders!'.
failing_case: The server returns 500, the network drops, or CORS blocks the call. The agent sees 'Refunded N orders!' and tells the customer the refund is done. No money moved. The rejected promise is unhandled.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the parsed result or throw. In app.js show the toast only on a confirmed success and show an error with a retry on failure. Send an idempotency key.

title: Customer name, id, total and status are written into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS)
evidence: Driven: an order whose customer.name is set window.__x=1 on render. The same string handling applies to o.id (attribute context) and o.status (class). The page holds the bearer key in a global, so the script can read it.
failing_case: A customer registers as . When an agent opens the dashboard the script runs and sends the key out, or posts refunds.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or escape every value). Validate status against the known list before using it as a class. Do not build the table with innerHTML += in a loop.

title: The main action, Refund selected, is a span: not focusable, no role, not operable by keyboard
evidence: Driven: tabIndex is -1 and tagName SPAN. Tab never reaches it. WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 (level A). It also has no disabled state when nothing is selected (app.js:50).
failing_case: A keyboard or screen reader user checks orders and cannot trigger the refund at all.
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn"> with a visible focus style and disabled until at least one order is selected.

quote: - **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the key never leaves the server; the key is in client JavaScript
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key and api.js:6 and 11 send it from the browser.
failing_case: A reviewer or buyer reads 'Secure' and relies on it. The key is visible in the page source.
remediation: Fix the code first (move the key server-side), then keep the claim. Until then remove it.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README accessibility claim is false, and 2.5.5 is Level AAA, not part of AA
evidence: Findings above: removed focus outlines (styles.css:19), contrast under 4.5:1 (styles.css:9), a span as the main action (index.html:19), unlabelled inputs. Pager buttons are padding 2px 4px, font 12px (styles.css:18), about 20 px tall, nowhere near 44 px. Criterion 2.5.5 Target Size is AAA in WCAG 2.1 (2.5.8, 24 px, is the AA one, in 2.2).
failing_case: A buyer or auditor relies on the stated WCAG 2.1 AA conformance and 44 px targets; the page fails both.
remediation: Remove the claim until it is measured, or fix the page and then state the criteria correctly (2.1 AA, with 44 px as an AAA goal).

quote: the Team plan is $15 per seat; 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: README pricing arithmetic is wrong: 12 seats x $15 x 12 months at 20% off is $1,728, not $1,440
evidence: 12 x 15 = 180 a month; x 12 = 2,160 a year; x 0.8 = 1,728. $1,440 equals 8 months of 180 (a 33% discount), or 12 x 120. Recomputed.
failing_case: A customer quoted $1,440 a year is charged or promised $288 less than the stated price and discount imply.
remediation: State $1,728 a year (or change the discount to match $1,440) and compute the figure from one constant. Pricing does not belong in a README for an order dashboard.

quote: - Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README claims refund confirmation that the code does not have
evidence: app.js:49-52 sends the POST on the first click; no confirm exists. Driven: one click sent the request.
failing_case: A reader assumes a safety step exists and so grants refund access more widely.
remediation: Implement the confirmation (see the app.js:49 finding) or delete the line.

title: getOrders never checks res.ok or the shape, and load() has no catch; a failed fetch leaves a stale screen with no message
evidence: Driven: with the orders endpoint answering 500 and {"error":"x"}, the console logged 'orders is not iterable' and the stats cards kept their previous values. A network error rejects the promise unhandled (app.js:41).
failing_case: The API returns 401 or 500 during a search. The agent sees old orders as if current and no error. A body that is not an array throws in renderStats.
remediation: Check res.ok and Array.isArray, throw a typed error, catch it in load(), and show an error state with a retry. Keep the last good data marked as stale.

title: Page numbering is off by one: page starts at 1 but the slice starts at page*10, so the first 10 orders are never shown on load
evidence: Driven with 25 orders: the first view showed C10 (order index 10) as the first row. Orders 0-9 are only reachable by pressing Prev to page 0, which the label shows as 'Page 0'.
failing_case: Open the dashboard with 25 orders. The newest 10 orders are missing from the first view and the user does not know.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or start page at 0 and display page + 1.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured 10 px dot with no text
evidence: styles.css:16-17 colours the dot red, green or yellow and nothing else names the status. WCAG 1.4.1 and 1.1.1.
failing_case: A colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded (the red/green pair), and a screen reader reads an empty cell.
remediation: Put the status word in the cell (visible text) and keep the dot as decoration with aria-hidden.

title: Unchecking a row never removes it from selected, and checking twice adds duplicates, so refunds go out for orders the user deselected
evidence: Driven: check, uncheck, check on one row gave selected ['10','10']; after an uncheck it was still ['10','10']. The POST body was {"ids":["10","10","10"]} and the toast said 3 orders.
failing_case: An agent ticks order 7 by mistake, unticks it, and ticks order 9. selected is [7, 9]. Refund sends both and refunds order 7 for real money.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id: add on check, delete on uncheck. Re-apply checked state on every render. Compute the count from the Set. Show the exact orders in a confirmation before sending.

title: Every keystroke fires a request and responses are applied in arrival order, so a slow old response overwrites a newer one
evidence: app.js:45 runs load() on every input event, with no debounce, abort or sequence check. app.js:41 assigns whichever response arrives last to `orders`, then renders. Each request also fetches the full list (no server-side paging, api.js:6).
failing_case: Type 'ab': the request for 'a' returns after the one for 'ab'. The search box says 'ab' but the table shows the results for 'a'. Selected ids from the earlier view stay in `selected`.
remediation: Debounce input by about 250 ms, give each request an AbortController or a sequence number, and ignore stale responses.

title: Refund runs on a single click with no confirmation, although README.md:9 says refunds are confirmed
evidence: No confirm, dialog or undo anywhere in app.js or index.html. Driven: one click sent the POST.
failing_case: A stray click on a destructive, money-moving action sends the refund immediately.
remediation: Add a confirmation step that names the count and total, with an explicit Refund N orders button and a Cancel.

title: Search, status filter and row checkboxes have no accessible name; the placeholder is the only label
evidence: index.html:17-18 has no label or aria-label on #q or #status; app.js:32 renders checkboxes with no label. The first th (index.html:21) is empty. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2 and 4.1.2.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'checkbox' with no purpose; a user cannot tell which order a checkbox selects.
remediation: Add <label> or aria-label to #q and #status, and aria-label="Select order {id}" on each checkbox. Give the first th visually hidden text.

title: Text colours fail 4.5:1 contrast: card labels, pager buttons, eyebrow
evidence: Computed: #aaa on #fff is 2.32:1 (.lbl); #aaa on #F4F1EA is 2.06:1 (button, styles.css:18, 12 px); #c7c2f0 on the #6366f1 and #8b5cf6 gradient is 2.64:1 and 2.50:1 (styles.css:4); white on #8b5cf6 (.refund, styles.css:12) is 4.23:1. WCAG 1.4.3.
failing_case: A user with low vision or a glare on the screen cannot read the labels, the Prev and Next buttons or the Refund button.
remediation: Use text colours of at least 4.5:1 (for example #595959 on white), darken the purple to #6d28d9 or darker for white text, and set the labels to 12 px or more.

title: The table is a fixed 1000 px wide, so the page scrolls sideways on a phone
evidence: Driven at 390 px: documentElement.scrollWidth was 1024. The cards (repeat(3,1fr), styles.css:6) and the toolbar also do not wrap.
failing_case: On a phone the user must pan sideways to reach the Status column and the Refund control.
remediation: Use width:100% with a wrapper that has overflow-x:auto, collapse the cards to one column below about 600 px, and let the toolbar wrap.

title: Focus indicators are removed from buttons, inputs and selects with no replacement
evidence: No :focus-visible rule exists in styles.css. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through the search box, filter, checkboxes and Prev/Next cannot see where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule or replace it with a :focus-visible outline of at least 3:1 contrast and 2 px.

title: Query is put into the URL without encoding, so the user can inject parameters
evidence: Driven: typing a b"&q=1# requested /orders?q=a%20b%22&q=1 (the browser dropped the # part). The injected second q reached the server.
failing_case: A search for 'Smith & Sons' or 'a&status=refunded' is sent as a different query and returns wrong rows.
remediation: Build the URL with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent for both values.

title: Tax rate, loyalty discount and revenue rules live inside a render function, and the figures disagree with the table
evidence: app.js:9-17 hard-codes 8.25% tax and a 10% gold discount in renderStats. The table shows the raw o.total (app.js:32) while revenue shows a discounted, taxed value; avg divides by all orders including pending (app.js:18). In the driven run, 25 orders of 100-124 gave a revenue far below the visible totals. Money rules are enforced only in the browser.
failing_case: A gold customer's $100 order shows as $100 in the table and counts as $97.43 in revenue. The finance figure on screen cannot be reconciled with the rows beside it.
remediation: Move the revenue rule to one pure, tested function (or the server, which owns tax and discount). The view should only display the result. Define whether pending orders count in the average.

title: Empty result shows '$NaN' as the average order
evidence: Driven: with an empty list the cards read '$0.00 REVENUE 0 ORDERS $NaN AVG ORDER'. This is also the first screen for a new account.
failing_case: Search for a name that matches nothing: the average card reads $NaN and the table is blank with no empty-state text.
remediation: Guard the zero case (show a dash) and add an empty-state message that says what to do next.

title: Page total uses floor, and Prev and Next are not bounded
evidence: Driven with 25 orders: label 'Page 1 of 2' (needs 3), Next twice reached 'Page 3 of 2' with 0 rows, Prev three times reached 'Page 0'. With 0 orders it reads 'Page 1 of 0'. page also is not reset when the search changes (app.js:45).
failing_case: Go to page 3, type a search that returns 5 results: an empty table with no message.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page in range, disable Prev and Next at the ends, and reset page to the first on a new query.

title: The toast is not announced and never goes away
evidence: No role=status or aria-live on #toast. app.js:51 sets display:block and nothing hides it. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
failing_case: A screen reader user presses refund and hears nothing; a sighted user sees a stale 'Refunded' message forever, even after a later failed attempt.
remediation: Add role="status" (or aria-live="polite") and clear or hide the message after a timeout or on the next action. Use role=alert for errors.

quote: button { border: 0; background: none; color: #aaa; padding: 2px 4px; font-size: 12px; }
title: Prev and Next are tiny, borderless, grey text buttons
evidence: Driven: Prev measured 32.7 x 18 px; checkboxes are 13 x 13 px. WCAG 2.5.8 is 24 px in 2.2 and 2.5.5 (44 px) is AAA. The buttons also have no border or hover state, so they do not read as controls.
failing_case: On a phone the paging controls are hard to hit and look like captions.
remediation: Give the buttons a visible border or fill, at least 24 px (preferably 44 px) of target size, and hover and disabled states.

quote: .toast { display: none; position: fixed; bottom: 16px; right: 16px; background: #111; color: #fff; padding: 12px; border-radius: 12px; animation: pop 1s infinite alternate; }
title: The toast pulses forever and ignores prefers-reduced-motion
evidence: animation: pop 1s infinite alternate with no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rule anywhere in styles.css. WCAG 2.2.2 (A), since it moves for over 5 s beside other content.
failing_case: A user with a vestibular disorder or attention difficulty gets a throbbing box that cannot be stopped while reading the table.
remediation: Remove the infinite pulse, or wrap it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and limit it to a single run.

quote: td:nth-child(2) { max-width: 120px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }
title: Customer names are cut at 120 px with no ellipsis or full-name access
evidence: The rule applies nowrap and overflow: hidden with no text-overflow: ellipsis and no title attribute (app.js:32).
failing_case: 'Wolfeschlegelsteinhausenbergerdorff & Sons Ltd' is silently cut at 120 px, and two similar long names look identical when the operator picks which to refund.
remediation: Allow wrapping, or add text-overflow: ellipsis plus a title or tooltip with the full name, and widen the column.
